editorial.headline: Eyewear Retail: Open Nationally, Closed to PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity spans retail sales of eyewear and optical products, but Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium prevents foreign-investment registration there today.
editorial.body:
A foreign investor cannot register this eyewear-retail activity as PMA in Bali today. That is the practical starting point, even though the national position is fully open to foreign investment. The distinction matters because the activity itself is straightforward and familiar: retailing a range of eyewear products, from vision-correction glasses and sunglasses or light-filtering glasses to contact lenses, soft lenses, and spectacle frames. It also includes optical specialists whose work includes selling glasses.

This is therefore a retail activity centred on the customer’s choice, fitting, and purchase of optical goods. Its scope is broad enough to accommodate both everyday eyewear and products connected with vision assistance, while expressly including the retail role of an optical expert. The record places the activity within direct sales, and opens it across every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That breadth describes who may register it by scale; it does not alter the separate foreign-investment treatment that applies in Bali.

Nationally, the code is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In other words, the national framework permits full foreign ownership for this activity. The governing PMA source recorded for that position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a founder assessing the national market, this is an open category rather than one subject to a stated foreign-equity cap below full ownership.

Bali reaches a different operational result. At the Besar scale, the OSS risk classification is Rendah or Menengah-Rendah across every scope of this activity. Bali’s rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide and permanently, and the resulting Bali status is BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO. The record ties that block to the Bali moratorium of May 13, 2026. So the national permission remains real, but it does not create a route for PMA registration in Bali while that island-wide moratorium applies. For this activity, the honest reading is simple: nationally open to full foreign ownership; unavailable for PMA registration in Bali today.
editorial.pullQuote: National permission does not create a route for PMA registration in Bali while the island-wide moratorium applies.
